contexts.text: When he desired to eat, nothing was offered him but dirt.
The miry places and the marshes () = things inapplicable and impure.
Enter into the mire, and tread the clay ().
Out of the mire of clay ().
As the potter treadeth the mire ().
To enter into the mire = into falsity; to tread the clay = evil.
The streets of those cities are ankle-deep in filth, and the houses unclean to the extent that they stink.
He was long in that dirty city... where the streets are nothing but dirt and mud... and where he had been fed with nothing but dirt...

It was granted to say to him, that these (treasures) are nothing, like earthly dirt; so that if he had a chamber full of such golden things, or if he had another full of mud and dirt, the one would be of no more value than the other... He said, that... such things are sometimes turned into dirt...
The mire of the streets () = falsities.
Those who cannot be reformed because they are in the falsities of evil, are signified by, The miry places and the marshes which are not healed, and go away into salt ().
And the miry clay signifies the evil of life.
The mire of the streets signifies that falsity.
